content.text:
The pattern matches **mp-1217913 (TaTiAlO6)**, a trirutile-type structure, as a single phase; no second phase is needed. The match rests on the three lowest-angle peaks; I only checked the higher-angle peaks roughly.

Observed peak positions, read from the data grid:
- A moderate peak at about 20.1° (intensity 31).
- A peak at about 21.9° (intensity 37).
- The strongest peak at 27.55° (intensity 100).
- Further peaks near 36.6° and around 41.5°.

From the TaTiAlO6 cell as given (a = 4.627 Å, c = 8.934 Å):
- (002) is expected at d = 4.47 Å, about 19.9°.
- (101) is expected at d = 4.11 Å, about 21.6°.
- (110) is expected at d = 3.27 Å, about 27.2°.

All three observed peaks sit slightly high, consistent with a cell about 1% smaller in both a and c. Refitting from the observed peaks gives a ≈ 4.575 Å and c ≈ 8.83 Å. With these values:
- (101) moves to 21.86°, matching the observed 21.9°.
- (113) falls at about 41.4°, consistent with the peak near 41.5°.
- (103) falls at about 36.3°, a little below the observed 36.6°.

So all main reflections index on the rutile-derived TaTiAlO6 cell. Because every peak shifts by the same proportion, a uniform contraction is a plausible explanation.

None of the other candidates was checked in detail. Their cells would not naturally give the 20°/21.9°/27.55° sequence with the strongest peak at the rutile (110) position.
